- E024 — Xi’s December 2023 integrity directive. Xinhua reports Xi chaired the Politburo self-criticism meeting and required officials to maintain integrity, self-discipline, and strict rules for family members and staff in anti-corruption efforts (lines 170–172). This is direct evidence of Xi’s stated position, not proof of personal honesty or compliance. Links: `7B.1`, `7B.2`, `7B.3`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`. [Source](https://www.idcpc.gov.cn/english2023/ttxw_5749/202312/t20231226_163194.html)

- E025 — Removal of Qin Gang and Li Shangfu. AP reported in October 2023 that both were Xi-era appointees removed amid opaque explanations; analysts interpreted the removals as enforcing obedience or eliminating rivals, while noting uncertainty over corruption, personal conduct, or political conflict (lines 1843–1850, 1870–1894). This supports institutional accountability/opacity and appointment-risk evidence, not Xi’s personal self-dealing. Links: `7B.4`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.9`, `8B.3`, `8B.9`. [Source](https://apnews.com/article/china-politics-xi-jinping-foreign-relations-0b9a867861c719456778bf5a8eee95ca)

- E026 — April 2023 Taiwan exercises and escalation options. CSIS reports that China’s April exercises rehearsed joint operations and possible blockade elements; unlike 2022, no ballistic missiles were fired over Taiwan, and simultaneous economic/diplomatic engagement continued (lines 281–305). This provides independent event analysis and mitigating evidence of calibrated escalation, but does not establish Xi’s personal order. Links: `2B.1`, `2B.2`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.8`, `2B.10`. [Source](https://www.csis.org/analysis/analyzing-chinas-escalation-after-taiwan-president-tsais-transit-through-united-states)
